chunks: Ibn al-Jawzi states in Al-Muntazam (vol. 8, p. 11):

[He is] the Sheikh of the Imamiyya and their scholar; he authored works according to their school of thought, and among his students was al-Murtada. Ibn al-Mu'allim had a scholarly debate session at his home — in Darb Rabah — which all scholars attended. He had standing with the regional princes by virtue of their inclination toward his school of thought.

key_terms.الْإِمَامِيَّةِ: the Imamiyya — the Twelver Shia community and their juridical-theological school
key_terms.الْمُرْتَضَى: al-Murtada — Sharif al-Murtada (Ali ibn al-Husayn, d. 436 AH), foremost student of al-Mufid and leading Shia theologian-jurist
key_terms.مَنْزِلَةٌ: standing, rank, and prestige — here denoting socio-political influence and honor
key_terms.نَظَرٍ: scholarly inquiry and dialectical disputation (kalam); naẓar denotes rigorous rational examination in classical Islamic thought

ai.seo_question: What did Ibn al-Jawzi record in Al-Muntazam about Sheikh al-Mufid's scholarly leadership, his student al-Murtada, and his debate sessions in Baghdad?
ai.summary: Ibn al-Jawzi, the eminent Hanbali historian, records in Al-Muntazam that Sheikh al-Mufid — referred to as Ibn al-Mu'allim — was the foremost scholar of the Imamiyya in Baghdad, with al-Murtada among his most distinguished students. He held regular scholarly debate sessions (majlis al-naẓar) at his home in the Darb Rabah quarter of Baghdad, attended by scholars of every background, and wielded political influence with the Buyid regional princes owing to their inclination toward his school of thought.
